result.title: Hawkeye: Reading Illegible Text with Vision Language Models
result.summary: While modern Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have been remarkably successful in general scene text recognition, they consistently struggle with the long-tail distribution of text that is degraded by motion blur or low resolution. These limitations are particularly apparent in egocentric applications like smart glasses, where text is often captured in noisy environments. In this paper, we introduce the \textbf{BSTRB} (Blurry Scene Text Recognition Benchmark), a novel benchmark of 8,398 noisy image samples with high-fidelity annotations derived from 1,699 real-world video sequences. To support this, we present \textbf{Hawkeye}, a VLM fine-tuned on BSTRB to read and reason about illegible text by leveraging contextual priors and pixel-level alignment. Our results show that \name matches much larger VLMs on BSTRB overall and exceeds them on text at or below 20 pixels, in a single pass suited to real-time deployment. We characterize the resolution at which current VLMs begin to fail.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 BSTRB 基准（由 1,699 段真实视频构建的 8,398 张模糊或低分辨率文本图像），并微调出 Hawkeye，利用上下文先验与像素级对齐读取难以辨认的文本，同时刻画当前 VLM 开始失效的分辨率阈值。
AI.relevance_reason: 对退化文本的细粒度视觉细节保留与失效分辨率的刻画，可供核查 visual evidence 质量、像素级对齐及「何时看不清」的诊断线索；但其单次前向的识别范式与 latent 推理状态生成关联较弱。
